quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket for motorcycle riding, you should look for one that is:

options.text: Black or another dark color.
Warm.
Made of leather or synthetic materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather or synthetic materials.
questions.explanation: Wear a protective jacket when riding a motorcycle. Choose one made of leather or sturdy synthetic material. It should cover your arms completely, fit snugly, and allow you to move freely. Integrated body armor offers the best protection.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use only your front brake.
Use only your rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply controlled pressure to both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: The best way to avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle trip is to:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to rest.
Ride as fast as possible.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent breaks to rest.
questions.explanation: On a long trip, limit your riding time each day and take frequent rest breaks to avoid fatigue. Do not use artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue can occur when they wear off.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket, make sure it:

options.text: Fits loosely and flaps in the wind.
Fits snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Is not made of leather or another sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Choose pants and a jacket made of leather or another sturdy material. They should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but loosely enough to allow free movement.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Sneakers
Leather boots
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather boots
questions.explanation: Leather boots provide the best protection when riding. They should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead is likely to be slippery when wet.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster it leaves your body.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the faster alcohol builds up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol will still be in your body after an hour.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Get off the roadway.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let tailgaters pass. Speeding up may increase danger by encouraging them to continue tailgating at the higher speed.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself in the lane so other drivers can see you as early as possible.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes since it is light outside.
Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you better.
Be comfortable and wear shorts if it is hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright clothing when riding, even during the day, so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: What is a sign that your rear tire has gone flat?

options.text: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
You hear a loud noise.
You see air being released.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle's rear tire goes flat, the back may jerk or sway from side to side. If you feel this movement, stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What should you do when a tailgater is following you?

options.text: Let them pass.
Speed up.
Keep riding the same way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Speeding up will not help. They will likely just tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must stop completely.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop completely.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that lets you turn the way you want to go.

questions.question: What may happen if a motorcycle rider takes a turn too fast?

options.text: They will have better control of the motorcycle.
The ride will be more stable.
They may accidentally leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may accidentally leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to lose control. The motorcycle may cross into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: How is alcohol different from other substances?

options.text: It is absorbed into the bloodstream very quickly.
It must be digested before entering the bloodstream.
It can improve your riding ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is absorbed into the bloodstream very quickly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It goes directly through the stomach and small intestine walls into the bloodstream. This happens quickly and affects the brain fast.

questions.question: What gives you the best chance of surviving a crash?

options.text: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet.
Wearing a baseball cap.
Wearing comfortable shoes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet.
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards provides the best head and neck protection. Wearing a properly fastened, good-quality helmet is the single best thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: What should a good lane position do?

options.text: Help you see others and let them see you.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and let them see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and helps them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also keeps other drivers from trying to share your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What should you do when railroad crossing lights are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
Go slowly and be careful.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before going. Never try to race a train.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Yes, they have blind spots just like cars.
No, because motorcycles are smaller than cars.
No, mirrors are not required on motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they have blind spots just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: If there are hazards to your right, which side of your lane should you ride on?

options.text: Right
Left
Either side

questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: Position yourself in your lane to have the most space. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle for safety?

options.text: Before every ride.
Every week.
Once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always check your motorcycle for safety before you ride. Even small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than small problems on a car.

questions.question: Why should you use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection?

options.text: To check if drivers behind you see that you are stopping.
To watch for pedestrians ahead.
To look for dark clouds that may show bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check if drivers behind you see that you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors to see vehicles coming up behind you. Make sure the drivers notice you and respond to your actions when you stop.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, how should your arms be positioned?

options.text: Bent slightly so you can reach the handlebars easily.
Stretched straight out to reach the handlebars.
Bent at a 90-degree angle when reaching the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bent slightly so you can reach the handlebars easily.
questions.explanation: Your elbows should be bent slightly when you hold the handgrips. This lets you reach and turn the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: They are less dangerous than using either one alone.
They balance each other out.
Their effects can be stronger than using either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their effects can be stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it unsafe to ride. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: What should you check before every ride?

options.text: That your brake lights work properly.
That the paint is not peeling.
That your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: That your brake lights work properly.
questions.explanation: Do a safety check before every ride. Test your brakes to make sure each one turns on the brake lights.
